# Direct object macros in field expressions

The twenty projects in `cases/` match the complete selected AST/NODES/EDGES/FLOWS projection from Joern v4.0.555: 5,329 canonical lines including method separators. The preceding nested-field increment matched two of these cases. The production test compares every record after building through `Project`, `CFrontend`, and the standard pipeline; a second test checks repeated macro accesses and the following calls retain their own source lines.

For `#define Len len`, Joern lowers `p->Len` to the expanded field name while keeping `p->Len` as the access CALL's CODE. Replacements such as `values[1]` or `len + 1` can also change the surrounding expression shape. CDT assigns the first expression wholly inside that replacement to an INLINED `Len` wrapper, while access operators that include the receiver retain the original access spelling. This agrees with the pinned `MacroHandler.scala` location, parent, and one-use macro-offset selection, and is pinned by complete fresh graphs for single and multiple replacement operands.

The repair expands the object macro using the existing disabled-macro set and work budget, reparses the receiver plus replacement, and carries original source spelling into expression emission. It reuses the existing macro wrapper emitter for the replacement subexpression. Introduced index operands are collected with their receiver context so a global index receives its required proxy LOCAL and field names do not become phantom variables. No importer, declaration-type renderer, CFG, or reaching-definition solver changes are included.

Cases cover `.` and `->`, array receivers, aliases, object chains, replacements containing arithmetic and subscripts, parameter/global/macro index operands, assignments, repeated occurrences, and source locations. Independent review added complete pins for call-valued indices, direct and indirect recursive index replacements, and two sibling wrapper owners. Self-recursion and a function-like name used without arguments retain their previously exact graphs. The original 308-block corpus is unchanged and passes both committed and fresh live comparisons.

Six full nonconformant diagnostics remain in the new probe set. `declaration` expands the access correctly but still retains the original macro token in MEMBER metadata; the reference uses the expanded member name. `receiver_macro` and `receiver_control` expose a preexisting leading-receiver macro ownership/type gap: Joern makes `PTR(p)->len` the macro invocation, while Rust wraps only `PTR(p)`. `conditional_piece` exposes general field-expression wrapper typing, confirmed by `wrapper_control`, which produces identical mismatches before and after this increment. `quoted_piece` retains a preexisting `sizeof` CODE spacing difference. The controls use no field macro and establish the broader boundaries independently. All before/candidate outputs and full differences are retained. This increment does not claim complete field-macro, aggregate-declaration, or general macro ownership parity.

`evidence/direct-nested-field/` also replays the preceding increment's complete `#define Len dl.len` / `p->Len` diagnostic against the new binary. All method ASTs now match; the unfiltered graph still differs in the existing nested-member TYPE scaffold. Its fresh live reference and raw-output provenance remain in the sibling `field-macros` fixture, with hashes recorded here. This historical replay is separate from the twenty-six new live projects.

The four `oracle/` packs preserve the scripts, raw stdout/stderr and invocation receipts for all twenty-six isolated inputs. Their projection is the shared `oracle.sc` with only an isolated-project driver. To reproduce a pack, assemble its recorded input cases from `cases/` and `diagnostics/`, then run the script with `--param inputPath=<directory>` in a fresh working directory using the pinned runtime and JDK 21.0.12. Extract each `CASE|` section, removing only the `AST|` prefix. No graph records are filtered and no expected graphs are edited by hand. The existing newline text encoding remains noninjective.

`measurement.json` binds all inputs, references, raw outputs, source and binaries. Before results use the frozen nested-field binary; candidate results were replayed after freezing the new source/binary pair. Validation covers 288 relevant Rust tests, formatting, strict workspace Clippy, and both 308-block gates. These small fixture timings establish reproducibility, not a whole-project performance claim.
